title: P1.11a2 Compose the authenticated durable goal-brief writer
description: Consume the shared goal-brief contract at the existing goal.create production seam. Replace caller-carried goal authority payloads with normalized prose plus server-derived project/principal/run/budget/readiness facts, persist the brief on the goal's durable GoalCreated row, and preserve byte-proven replay.
definitionOfDone: Verify-or-block first: re-measure the landed goal-brief contract, the existing goal.create store writer, and the GoalCreated budget/catalog consumers; also prove apps/daemon declares @moe/contracts in package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml and a temporary bare-specifier import typechecks.

The authenticated production goal.create payload accepts only title and instructions; project and principal come from authentication, planningRunRef and budgetAccountRef are derived uniquely from the target goal, and ProjectReadyWitness is derived from the committed project activation rather than caller fields or a fixed live run.

One accepted command durably records the exact normalized brief on the target goal's GoalCreated fact and returns a stable durable decision receipt; malformed admitted fields refuse GOAL_BRIEF_INPUT_INVALID at DAEMON_INGRESS with no decision or event mutation.
Former authority payload keys and other hostile extras on the real command seam refuse INPUT_INVALID at PAYLOAD_SHAPE; tests pin both the code and refusing stage and prove no durable mutation.

A byte-identical retry under the same authenticated command identity replays without a second write even when the daemon clock advances; same identity with changed brief bytes refuses BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_BYTES_CONFLICT at DAEMON_PREREQUISITE.
Focused daemon tests run standalone with exit 0 and nonzero Vitest count lines, and a production refusal mutation makes the named assertion red before restoration.

Do not change the generic HTTP/MCP ordering or create a second goal lifecycle reducer.

implementationPlan.description: Prove the two refusal fences SEPARATELY (DoD 3 and 4), because they are the pair most easily confused. DIVERGENCE REQUIREMENT: no case may carry BOTH a malformed brief and an extra key, because such a fixture cannot tell you which fence answered; each case must be constructed so exactly one mechanism can refuse it. Every case asserts the exact code AND the refusing stage, and asserts NO durable mutation occurred — read the store back rather than trusting the return value. implementationPlan.description: Prove byte-identical replay (DoD 5) in the same test file. Arm one: submit an accepted command, ADVANCE THE DAEMON CLOCK explicitly, resubmit byte-identical payload under the same authenticated command identity, and assert it replays with NO second write — assert the durable event count is unchanged, not merely that the second call returned ok. Advancing the clock is the point of the arm: without it a naive dedupe on timestamp would pass and prove nothing. Arm two: same command identity with CHANGED brief bytes must refuse BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_BYTES_CONFLICT at DAEMON_PREREQUISITE, again with no durable mutation.
implementationPlan.note:
Both replay arms added to goal-services.test.ts (26 passed / 26).

ARM ONE — byte-identical retry under the SAME authenticated command identity, with the daemon clock explicitly advanced from 2026-08-08T00:00:00.000Z to 2026-08-09T12:34:56.789Z. Asserts disposition REPLAYED, authority DURABLE_DECISION, and — the evidence that matters — that store.readEvents(GOAL_ID) is still length 1 and the decision count is unchanged, rather than merely that the second call returned ok. It also pins that the replayed receipt carries the FIRST command's decidedAt, so a writer that re-decided under the new clock could not pass. The clock advance is load-bearing: the replay fence digests {kind, payload} and deliberately excludes the decided-at reading, so a writer that deduplicated on the timestamp would pass a same-clock arm while proving nothing.

ARM TWO — same command identity, changed brief bytes (a different title, same shape): refuses BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_BYTES_CONFLICT at DAEMON_PREREQUISITE with advisoryOnly true. Reads the store back: decision count unchanged, still exactly one event, and the stored brief is still the FIRST command's brief — a conflict that quietly overwrote the fact would still leave one event behind, so the event count alone would not have caught it.
